questions.question: What is the key difference between the Anthropic Client SDK and the Claude Agent SDK?
options: The Client SDK uses Claude 3; the Agent SDK uses Claude 4
The Client SDK provides raw Messages API access; the Agent SDK provides the full harness (tools, MCP, hooks, subagents, session store)
The Client SDK is for Python; the Agent SDK is for TypeScript
The Client SDK is free; the Agent SDK requires a paid plan
questions.explanation: The Client SDK (anthropic) gives you raw Messages API access — you own the loop, tools, and state. The Agent SDK (claude-agent-sdk) provides the Claude Code harness as a library: built-in tool execution, MCP connections, hooks, subagent spawning, and session store.

questions.question: What are the two purposes of subagents in the Claude Agent SDK?
options: Testing and production
Parallelization (run independent work concurrently) and context isolation (subagents use their own context window)
CPU-bound and I/O-bound tasks
Tool calls and memory operations
questions.explanation: Subagents serve two documented purposes: parallelization (run 20 independent tasks as 20 concurrent subagents) and context isolation (each subagent uses its own context window; only results return to the orchestrator, preserving the orchestrator's budget).

questions.question: What are the session store operations in the Python Claude Agent SDK?
options: read, write, update, delete
append, load, list_sessions, delete (with cascade), list_subkeys
push, pop, peek, clear
get, set, remove, enumerate
questions.explanation: The Python SDK session store provides: append(session_id, message), load(session_id), list_sessions(), delete(session_id) with cascade to subagent sessions, and list_subkeys(session_id) to list subagent keys.

questions.question: What lifecycle hooks does the Claude Agent SDK provide?
options: OnStart, OnStop, OnError
PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, PreCompact, Stop, Notification
Before, During, After
Initialize, Execute, Finalize
questions.explanation: The Claude Agent SDK provides lifecycle hooks: PreToolUse, PostToolUse (gate or audit tool calls), SessionStart, SessionEnd (setup/teardown), UserPromptSubmit (act on user input), PreCompact (before context compaction), Stop (cleanup on exit), and Notification (side-channel alerts).

questions.question: How does Claude Managed Agents differ from the self-hosted Claude Agent SDK?
options: Managed Agents use a different model
Managed Agents is Anthropic-hosted for long-running async work with built-in prompt caching and compaction; self-hosted gives full control
Managed Agents only support Python; self-hosted supports all languages
Managed Agents are free; self-hosted requires a license
questions.explanation: Claude Managed Agents (beta header managed-agents-2026-04-01) is Anthropic-hosted for long-running async work with built-in prompt caching and compaction. The trade is less control for managed infrastructure.

questions.question: What is the W3C trace context feature of the Claude Agent SDK?
options: A way to share traces with W3C committee for review
OTel spans active on the caller propagate into CLI subprocess so the whole multi-process trace appears as one trace in the backend
A standard for formatting trace IDs in log files
A protocol for transmitting agent state between sessions
questions.explanation: The Claude Agent SDK propagates OTel spans from the caller into the CLI subprocess via W3C trace context headers. The entire multi-process trace (orchestrator + subagents) appears as one unified trace in your observability backend.
